question: Family planning means:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. deciding freely the number and spacing of children by using safe methods

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Family planning is the voluntary and informed choice of the number and spacing of children using safe and acceptable methods

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — limiting every family to one child: A one-child rule is not what family planning means

C — avoiding marriage altogether: Avoiding marriage is not a method of family planning

D — using medicines to cure infertility: Fertility treatment is part of infertility care, not family planning

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: Family planning protects the health of the mother and child as much as it controls family size
option_2: deciding freely the number and spacing of children by using safe methods

question: The intrauterine device CuT 380A provides protection against pregnancy for:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. ten years

🧠 Clinical Rationale: CuT 380A is licensed for up to ten years of use and can also be used for emergency contraception

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — one year: Its useful life is far longer than a year

B — three months: Three months describes no intrauterine device

C — the whole of the woman's life: No device is licensed for life

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The device can be removed at any time and fertility returns promptly

question: Combined oral contraceptive pills prevent pregnancy mainly by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. inhibiting ovulation and thickening the cervical mucus

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The oestrogen and progestogen in combined pills suppress ovulation and make the cervical mucus hostile to sperm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — preventing implantation by a foreign body: A foreign body such as a coil prevents implantation

C — blocking the fallopian tubes: Pills do not block the tubes mechanically

D — destroying the sperm in the vagina: Pills do not act as a spermicide in the vagina

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: Pills must be taken daily at about the same time for reliable protection
option_2: inhibiting ovulation and thickening the cervical mucus

question: As an emergency contraceptive, the copper intrauterine device can be inserted:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. up to five days after unprotected intercourse

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The copper intrauterine device is the most effective emergency method and can be inserted up to five days after unprotected intercourse

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — only within two hours: Two hours is an impossibly short window

B — only after a missed period: It must be inserted before the next period is missed

D — only during menstruation: Insertion is not restricted to menstruation, though it is easier then

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: It also provides long-term contraception once inserted
option_3: up to five days after unprotected intercourse

question: A woman who has just delivered a healthy baby at term wants contraception before discharge. The postpartum IUCD can be inserted:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. within 48 hours of delivery, or after four to six weeks if missed

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Postpartum insertion is safe within 48 hours of delivery, and if that window is missed it is done after four to six weeks

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — only after six months: Waiting six months loses the opportunity for immediate protection

C — only during labour: Insertion during labour is not the recommended time

D — only after the first menstrual period: Insertion does not have to wait for the first period

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: Counsel the woman antenatally so that the decision is made before delivery
option_2: within 48 hours of delivery, or after four to six weeks if missed

question: Compared with female sterilisation, male sterilisation (vasectomy) has the advantage that it is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a shorter, simpler procedure under local anaesthesia with fewer complications

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vasectomy is a quick outpatient procedure under local anaesthesia with a low complication rate

❌ Why Not Other Options?

question: Apart from preventing pregnancy, the condom has the added advantage of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. protecting against sexually transmitted infections

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The condom is a barrier method that reduces the transmission of sexually transmitted infections including HIV

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — curing pelvic infection: A condom prevents, but does not cure, pelvic infection

C — making the periods lighter: Condoms do not influence the amount of menstrual bleeding

D — regulating the menstrual cycle: Condoms do not alter the menstrual cycle

question: The lactational amenorrhoea method is reliable only when:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the baby is exclusively breastfed, the mother is amenorrhoeic and the baby is under six months of age

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The method works only when all three conditions are met: exclusive breastfeeding, no menstruation and a baby under six months

A — the baby is given top feeds besides breast milk: Supplementary feeds reduce the hormonal suppression of ovulation

C — the mother has started menstruating again: Return of menstruation ends the method's reliability

D — the mother is breastfeeding occasionally after six months: Occasional breastfeeding after six months does not give protection

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: Another method should be started as soon as any of the three conditions fails

question: Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, pregnancy may be terminated on the woman's request up to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. twenty weeks of gestation, with later limits for special categories under the amended Act

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Act permits termination up to twenty weeks on the woman's request, with a higher limit for specified categories after the 2021 amendment

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — any time without any condition: Statutory conditions must always be satisfied

B — four weeks of gestation only: Four weeks is far below the legal limit

D — forty weeks of gestation at will: Termination on demand at any gestation is not permitted

question: The very first step in the care of a baby immediately after birth is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. dry the baby with a warm towel and cover the head to prevent heat loss

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Drying and covering the baby immediately prevent hypothermia and stimulate breathing within the first minute

❌ Why Not Other Options?

solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. increases the flow of blood and iron from the placenta to the baby

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Waiting to clamp the cord lets extra blood and iron pass to the baby, improving the haemoglobin and iron stores

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — reduces the birth weight: Delayed clamping does not reduce birth weight

C — prevents neonatal jaundice: Delayed clamping slightly increases bilirubin but does not prevent jaundice

D — has no effect on the baby: There is a real benefit to the newborn

question: A newborn is not breathing after drying and stimulation. The first step in resuscitation is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. open the airway in a neutral position and give positive pressure ventilation with a bag and mask

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The initial step in neonatal resuscitation is to open the airway and begin positive pressure ventilation with a self-inflating bag and mask at 40 to 60 breaths per minute

🔍 Key Clues: newborn

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give intravenous adrenaline: Drugs are considered much later in the algorithm

B — begin chest compressions at once: Compressions are started only if the heart rate stays below 60 per minute after effective ventilation

D — give oxygen by nasal prongs while observing: Merely observing wastes the golden minute

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Ventilation, not compressions, is the key to reviving a non-breathing newborn
option_3: open the airway in a neutral position and give positive pressure ventilation with a bag and mask
option_4: give oxygen by nasal prongs while observing

question: Which measure best prevents heat loss in a newborn on a labour room table?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. place the baby skin-to-skin on the mother and cover both with a warm blanket

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Skin-to-skin contact with a warm cover is the most effective and simple way to keep a newborn warm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — leave the baby on a cold metal tray while the mother is sutured: An unheated surface conducts heat away rapidly

C — bathe the baby immediately after birth: Immediate bathing causes major heat loss

D — keep the baby under a fan in a cool room: A fan increases heat loss by convection

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Keep the room warm and pre-warm towels and blankets before delivery
option_1: place the baby skin-to-skin on the mother and cover both with a warm blanket
option_2: leave the baby on a cold metal tray while the mother is sutured
option_4: keep the baby under a fan in a cool room

question: During neonatal resuscitation the heart rate is found to be 50 per minute after thirty seconds of effective ventilation. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. continue ventilation and begin chest compressions at 90 compressions per minute with a 3 to 1 ratio

🧠 Clinical Rationale: When the heart rate remains below 60 per minute despite good ventilation, chest compressions are begun with three compressions to one breath

🔍 Key Clues: 50 per minute

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give intravenous fluids: Intravenous fluids are not part of initial resuscitation

B — stop ventilation and start drugs only: Ventilation must continue along with compressions

D — wait another five minutes before any action: Waiting five minutes would cause hypoxic injury

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Reassess the heart rate every thirty seconds and stop compressions once it exceeds 60 per minute
option_3: continue ventilation and begin chest compressions at 90 compressions per minute with a 3 to 1 ratio
option_4: wait another five minutes before any action

question: The first breastfeed for a healthy newborn should be started:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. within one hour of birth

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Feeding within the first hour gives the baby colostrum, stabilises the blood sugar and reduces newborn deaths

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — after the first bath: Bathing should not delay the first feed

B — after the mother has slept for six hours: Waiting until the mother has slept deprives the baby of colostrum

D — after twelve hours: Twelve hours of delay risks hypoglycaemia and dehydration

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Support the mother to position and attach the baby correctly at the first feed
option_2: after the mother has slept for six hours

question: A newborn has good tone and a heart rate of 110 per minute but is gasping irregularly. The correct action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. provide positive pressure ventilation with a bag and mask

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Gasping or apnoeic breathing with a heart rate below 100 per minute requires assisted ventilation

🔍 Key Clues: newborn | 110 per minute

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — leave the baby with the mother without any support: The baby needs active support, not simple observation

B — start chest compressions: Compressions are not indicated when the heart rate is above 60 per minute

C — give free-flow oxygen and observe: Observation alone will not correct the irregular breathing

option_4: provide positive pressure ventilation with a bag and mask

question: To prevent infection of the umbilical stump in a home setting, the recommended measure is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. apply chlorhexidine to the cord stump for the first week

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Applying chlorhexidine to the cord stump in the first week reduces omphalitis and neonatal mortality

A — apply oil and cover the stump tightly: Oil and tight covering retain moisture and promote infection

solution:
